Associate Director, Maintenance

Location: This position is currently remote. A future transition to an on-site location on the U.S. East-Coast/Mid-West is anticipated as the project progresses, with an expected timeline in 2027. This is a full-time role with a Monday–Friday schedule from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

What you will get:

The full-time base annual salary for this position is expected to range between $174,000 to $203,000. In addition, below you will find a comprehensive summary of the benefits package we offer:

  • Performance-related bonus.

  • Medical, dental and vision insurance.

  • 401(k) matching plan.

  • Life insurance, as well as short-term and long-term disability insurance.

  • Employee assistance programs.

  • Paid time off (PTO).

Compensation for this role will be determined by the candidate’s qualifications, skills, experience, and relevant knowledge.

What will you do:

We are seeking an Associate Director, Maintenance to lead maintenance and reliability readiness activities for a U.S. growth investment project supporting small molecule drug substance manufacturing. This role will ensure the facility, equipment, utilities, process equipment, and maintenance systems are designed and implemented with long-term reliability, maintainability, mechanical integrity, and GMP compliance in mind. Working closely with Engineering, Operations, Automation, MSAT, and Quality, you will help establish the maintenance organization, systems, and processes required for successful site start-up and ongoing operations.

  • Provide maintenance and reliability leadership throughout facility design, construction, commissioning, qualification, and start-up activities

  • Develop maintenance strategies, including preventive, predictive, and reliability-centered maintenance programs to support long-term asset performance

  • Partner with Engineering and project teams to ensure maintainability, serviceability, accessibility, and lifecycle considerations are incorporated into facility and equipment design

  • Establish asset lifecycle management strategies, including spare parts plans, calibration programs, and equipment reliability initiatives

  • Support the selection, implementation, and optimization of CMMS and other maintenance technologies to enable effective planning and execution

  • Participate in commissioning, qualification, FAT/SAT, and operational readiness activities to ensure maintenance requirements are incorporated and validated

  • Define the future maintenance organization, including staffing plans, training requirements, operating procedures, and site support models

  • Identify and mitigate equipment reliability, maintenance, and operational readiness risks while providing updates and recommendations to project leadership

What we are looking for:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Facilities Management, Reliability Engineering, or a related technical discipline; advanced degree preferred

  • 10+ years of experience in maintenance, reliability, engineering, or technical operations within pharmaceutical or API manufacturing environments. Experience with HPAPI, complex chemical synthesis, or chemical process manufacturing is preferred.

  • Experience supporting major capital projects, facility start-ups, manufacturing expansions, greenfield or brownfield investments, or large-scale operational readiness initiatives

  • Strong knowledge of maintenance best practices, reliability engineering, asset lifecycle management, and equipment performance improvement

  • Experience with CMMS platforms, predictive maintenance technologies, reliability-centered maintenance (RCM), and maintenance planning systems

  • Understanding of GMP requirements related to equipment maintenance, calibration, qualification, documentation, and inspection readiness and mechanical integrity principles

  • Demonstrated experience supporting small molecule drug substance, API, or HPAPI manufacturing operations preferred

  • Experience supporting containment-intensive manufacturing environments (e.g., HPAPI containment, isolators, contained material handling) preferred

  • Experience within a multi-product API manufacturing or CDMO environment is preferred

  • Strong leadership, communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and stakeholders

  • Ability and willingness to transition to an East Coast or Midwest U.S. site location as project needs evolve

  • Travel: Willingness and ability to travel to EMEA and NA at approximately 25-30% of the time to meet business objectives

About Lonza

At Lonza, our people are our greatest strength. With 30+ sites across five continents, our globally connected teams work together every day to manufacture the medicines of tomorrow. Our core values of Collaboration, Accountability, Excellence, Passion and Integrity reflect who we are and how we work together. Everyone’s ideas, big or small, have the potential to improve millions of lives, and that’s the kind of work we want you to be part of.

Innovation thrives when people from all backgrounds bring their unique perspectives to the table. At Lonza, we offer equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. If you’re ready to help turn our customers’ breakthrough ideas into viable therapies, we look forward to welcoming you on board.

jobs.description:
Join the Tilt team

At Tilt, we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss. Our mobile-first products and machine learning-powered credit models look beyond credit scores, using over 250 real-time financial signals to recognize real potential. With millions of customers worldwide, we're not just changing how people access financial products — we're creating a new credit system that backs the working, whatever they're working toward.


The Opportunity: Controller

Tilt is looking for a Controller to lead our accounting operations and build the infrastructure to support public company readiness. Reporting to the Head of Accounting, you'll lead a team of accountants and be the operational backbone of our finance function, partnering closely with FP&A, Legal, and other stakeholders to ensure our financial house is built to last. This is a role for a hands-on leader who thrives on building — someone who wants their fingerprints on how a company scales.


How You'll Make an Impact

  • Own the Close: Lead all aspects of US accounting operations and consolidation, delivering accurate, timely financial statements in accordance with GAAP.

  • Build for Scale: Redesign the accounting operations from the ground up, establishing best practices, standardizing processes, and creating the infrastructure needed to support IPO readiness and beyond.

  • Strengthen the Control Environment: Design, implement, and maintain a robust system of internal controls that safeguards assets, ensures reporting integrity, and meets SEC and regulatory requirements.

  • Lead and Develop the Team: Manage and mentor a team of accountants, while also rolling up your sleeves as an individual contributor where needed.

  • Champion an Automation Mindset: Identify where AI and automation can uplevel the team — shifting work from manual preparation to high-judgment review and analysis.

  • Serve as a Key Financial Liaison: Coordinate with internal stakeholders, external auditors, regulators, and investors, ensuring clear and transparent communication on the company's financial position.


Why You're a Great Fit

  • Financial services background required — you've worked in a fintech or consumer credit environment and understand the nuanced accounting that comes with it.

  • 10+ years in accounting/finance, with experience in a leadership role; you're equally comfortable as a manager and as someone who still gets their hands dirty.

  • NetSuite power user — you can configure, optimize, and get the most out of the platform without outside help.

  • Operator at heart — you've rebuilt or stood up accounting operations before and know what "good" looks like for a company on the path to IPO.

  • Curious about automation — you don't need to be an AI expert, but you should be excited about what it means for the future of accounting and eager to bring that thinking to the team.

  • SQL familiarity is a plus — comfortable reading queries and working cross-functionally with data and FP&A teams.


Our Interview Process

  1. Initial recruiter call: A conversation to learn about your experience and what you're looking for in your next role.

  2. Hiring manager interview: A deeper discussion about your background and approach to solving challenges.

  3. Skills panel: Meet with Tilt team members to discuss your expertise and problem-solving approach through real-world scenarios.

  4. Leadership conversations: Conversations with our CFO and CEO to discuss our mission and how you could contribute to it (and how we can help you achieve your career goals along the way).

Don’t meet every qualification? We care about potential over your past. If you're bringing ambition and drive to what we're building, we want to hear from you.

What you'll get at Tilt

  • Virtual-first teamwork: The Tilt team is collaborating across 14 countries, 12 time zones, and counting. You’ll get started with a WFH office reimbursement.

  • Competitive pay: We're big on potential, and it's reflected in our competitive compensation packages and generous equity.

  • Complete support: Find flexible health plans at every premium level, and substantial subsidies that stand up to global standards.

  • Visibility is yours: You can count on direct exposure to our leadership team — we’re a team where good ideas travel quickly.

  • Paid global onsites: Magic happens IRL: we gather twice yearly to reconnect over shared meals or kayaking adventures. (We’ve visited Vail, San Diego, and Mexico City, to name a few.)

  • Impact is recognized: Growth opportunities follow your contributions, not rigid promotion timelines.

The Tilt Way

We're looking for people who chase excellence and impact. Those who stand behind their work, celebrating the wins and learning from the missteps equally. We foster an environment where every voice is valued and mutual respect is non-negotiable — brilliant jerks need not apply. We're in this together, working to expand access to fair credit and prove that people are incredible. When you join us, it's not just another day at the [virtual] office, you're helping millions of hardworking people reach better financial futures.

You’re pushing ahead in your career? We can get behind that. Join us in building the credit system that people deserve.

Compensation Range: $200K - $230K

jobs.excerpt: About AtlysOur mission is to enable every person on Earth to travel freely.
jobs.description:
About Atlys

Our mission is to enable every person on Earth to travel freely.

Travel should feel exciting. Instead, too much of it is still defined by paperwork, uncertainty, and processes that were never designed for travellers.

Atlys is changing that.

We’re building an AI-first platform that removes friction and uncertainty from travel. To date, we’ve processed visas for 1M+ travellers across 127 countries. But we’re still early.

The Role

We're looking for a City Scout to help build the most reliable database of work-friendly cafes for travellers across Central Asia & Caucasus.

You'll visit cafes across your assigned city, verify information like WiFi quality, internet speed, plug points and overall work-friendliness, and submit accurate data that powers a new Atlys product. Every visit directly improves the travel experience for thousands of users.

Hiring in: Baku, Tbilisi and Almaty.

The Job

  • Explore and discover great cafes: Visit assigned cafes across your city, experience them as a customer, and identify places that travellers would genuinely enjoy working from.

  • Collect high-quality on-ground data: Verify key details including WiFi availability, internet speed, passwords, plug points, seating, ambience and overall work-friendliness to ensure the information is accurate and reliable.

  • Contribute to a travel product used by thousands: Capture your observations by completing a short digital survey after every visit, helping build one of the world's most reliable databases of work-friendly cafes.

  • Cover your city efficiently: Plan your visits across assigned neighbourhood clusters to maximize coverage while maintaining consistency and quality.

  • Maintain exceptional data quality: Pay close attention to detail, validate every submission, and ensure the information travellers see on the Atlys app can be trusted.

The Ideal Candidate

You’ll likely thrive in this role if you:

  • Are a college student or have a flexible part-time schedule.

  • Enjoy exploring your city and discovering new places.

  • Have strong attention to detail and collect information accurately.

  • Are comfortable travelling independently within your city.

  • Own a smartphone and are reliable, proactive and self-driven.

What you can expect

Atlys is built by a small team with outsized ambition, high ownership, and an obsession with doing great work.

Here’s what you can expect:

  • Competitive compensation and equity so you participate in the value you help create.

  • Comprehensive health insurance covering you and your family, plus annual preventive health check-up on us.

  • A thoughtful leave policy with paid time off and company holidays, because great work also requires real time off.

  • Lunch, high tea and dinner at the office, so the basics are taken care of while we build together.

  • Learning & development credits to invest in courses, books, conferences and tools that help you get better at your craft.

  • Relocation support to make moving closer to the team as seamless as possible.

  • Great tools to do your best work, including high-spec equipment and software.

  • An office designed for more than just work, with pickleball, table tennis, PlayStation, an arcade game room, an F1 simulator and even a full flight simulator.

Our values shape how we make decisions, work together and build for travelers. The bar is high, the pace is fast, and the way we work is deliberate. Read them before you apply. If this environment energizes you, you’ll probably thrive here. If it doesn’t, it’s better to know that upfront.

Come build the intelligence layer for global travel

Ease is hiring an Account Executive to help manufacturers improve quality, safety, and operational performance through our category-leading plant floor audit platform.

In this role, you'll own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery through negotiation and close, while partnering with some of the world's leading manufacturing organizations. You'll join a growing team, sell a proven solution with strong market traction, and have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on both our customers and the company's continued growth.

Position Summary
As an Account Executive at Ease, you’ll own the full sales cycle for enterprise manufacturing prospects, from first conversation to signed contract. You’re the first face these organizations see, and the impression you leave sets the tone for everything that follows. You’ll build relationships across the org, from the plant floor to the C-suite, and you’ll understand the difference between the two audiences well enough to speak to both without changing your conviction.

In this role, you’ll work closely with Marketing, Customer Success, and Product to move qualified deals forward and hand off new customers in a way that sets them up to win. If you’re a hunter who also knows how to build trust, asks better questions than you give answers, and measures success by the deals that actually close: this one is for you.

Salary: $200k+ OTE

What You'll Do:
  • Prospect, qualify, and engage enterprise-level manufacturing organizations. You’re not waiting for leads to come to you. You know your ICP, you know where to find them, and you know how to earn the first conversation.
  • Build and manage a qualified pipeline. The majority of it will be self-sourced. Quality over volume. Know what’s real and what’s wishful, and have the discipline to tell the difference. A clean pipeline is a credible pipeline.
  • Run discovery that goes deeper than features and functions. Understand what a quality or safety problem actually costs the people in the room. Not just the business on paper, but the plant manager who’s been dealing with it for two years.
  • Deliver compelling product demonstrations that are tailored, not templated. The demo should feel like it was built for that customer, because it was. Show them their world in the product, not a generic walkthrough.
  • Partner with Marketing and Customer Success to move deals forward and hand off new customers in a way that sets them up for long-term success. The close isn’t the finish line. It’s the starting line.
  • Stay sharp on the manufacturing landscape: the pressures, the priorities, and the language of the people you’re selling to. The best reps in this space earn credibility on the plant floor, not just in the boardroom.
  • Own the full sales cycle. Prospecting through close. Negotiate with confidence, manage multiple stakeholders across the org, and drive deals to a decision, in either direction. Knowing when to walk away is part of the job.

Required Qualifications & Skills:
  • 3+ years of experience in a closing role, with a track record of winning new business in enterprise-level accounts. You know what it takes to move a complex deal and you’ve done it more than once.

  • Competitive and accountable, without needing external pressure to stay on track. You set your own standard, and it’s a high one. You also know when to walk away from the wrong deal and redirect your energy.
  • A consultative approach to discovery. You understand that the personal cost of a problem is just as important as the business case. You know how to find both, and you know how to connect them to the people making the decision.
  • Genuine curiosity about the manufacturing sector. You don’t need to be an industry veteran, but you need to be the kind of person who wants to understand how things are made, where the problems live, and what keeps a plant manager up at night.
  • Comfortable managing complex, multi-stakeholder deals with long cycles. You know how to keep momentum without pushing. You build relationships across the org, not just with the person who signs the paper.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce, Apollo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and ZoomInfo.

Ease digitally transforms plant floor audits around the world with EASE. The enterprise-grade mobile platform combines simplicity and efficiency with powerful performance insights, driving quality and safety on the plant floor.

Industry leaders, including Aston Martin, Dana, 3M, Tenneco, and Samsung, trust EASE to facilitate and analyze millions of plant floor audits every year. With deployments in over 40 countries, EASE supports more than 25 languages, solidifying its position as a category leader for quality management, as recognized by G2 and Gartner.

Headquartered in Irvine, California, Ease. is a dynamic company that recently secured a growth investment from Luminate Capital Partners, further fueling its robust growth trajectory.

What We Offer
At Ease, we foster a culture built on respect, humility, and collaboration. We value work-life balance as a core principle, help ing ensure you can thrive both professionally and personally. And yes—we believe work should be fun, too.

Growth and development are part of our DNA. We are committed to investing in your career through ongoing training, mentorship, and a clearly defined path forward. Whether you are sharpening existing skills or exploring new ones, you will have opportunities to learn and advance.

We prioritize the well-being and happiness of our team. In addition to a competitive compensation package, we offer a generous and comprehensive suite of benefits designed to support your health and peace of mind.

Here’s a look at what you can expect:
  • Health Coverage: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans
  • Life & AD&D Insurance: Financial protection for you and your loved ones
  • Unlimited Paid Time Off: Time to recharge and rest when you need it
  • 401(k) with Employer Match: Plan for your future with confidence through our matched retirement savings program
At Ease, we believe that when our employees are supported, inspired, and empowered, everyone wins.

Overview

Who We Are

Dendreon is pioneering the future of immunotherapy. For over a decade, we have harnessed the power of the patient’s own immune system to fight cancer. Our flagship cellular therapy and growing pipeline are grounded in a simple belief: the immune system holds the key to transforming cancer care.

Headquartered in Seal Beach, California, with major operations in Union City, GA and Seattle, WA, we are now expanding our impact through contract manufacturing, patient operations, and commercial excellence in cellular immunotherapies. We are a purpose-driven organization that puts patients first and raises the bar every day.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Associate Director, Market Access & Reimbursement to lead strategy and execution for optimal patient access, reimbursement, and commercial success of our innovative oncology therapies. This critical leadership role will shape how payers, providers, GPO’s, distributors, and patients experience Dendreon’s products across all sites of care.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

  • Align with leadership in Commercial department to develop and execute comprehensive market access and reimbursement strategies to secure favorable coverage, coding, and payment for Dendreon’s cellular immunotherapies.
  • Lead pricing, contracting, and gross-to-net activities, including payer and channel negotiations, government pricing compliance (Medicare Part B/D, Medicaid, 340B), and forecasting support.
  • Drive buy-and-bill and site-of-care strategies across urology, community oncology, academic centers, and hospital outpatient settings.

  • Lead and develop the Field Reimbursement team and patient support programs (HUB services, prior authorization support, patient assistance).

  • Partner closely with Commercial, Medical Affairs, Finance, Legal, Compliance, and Government Affairs to align market access efforts with brand strategy and product launches.
  • Attend national and regional conferences, using the opportunity to engage with thought leaders and important customers
  • Monitor reimbursement trends, resolve access barriers, and deliver insights to support business performance and patient access.
  • Represent Dendreon in payer and provider engagements, delivering compelling access strategies and business reviews.

Qualifications

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree required; MBA, MPH, PharmD, or other advanced degree preferred.
  • 10–12+ years of progressive experience in Market Access, Managed Markets, Reimbursement, or Commercial Strategy within the pharmaceutical/biotechnology industry.
  • 5+ years of people leadership experience, including leading Field Reimbursement, Market Access, or Patient Support teams.
  • Strong experience with specialty pharmaceuticals, oncology, biologics, and buy-and-bill products.
  • Deep knowledge of Medicare Part B and Part D, payer contracting, coding/coverage strategies, and government pricing programs.
  • Proven track record supporting product launches and commercialization in complex reimbursement environments.
  • Experience managing relationships with payers, specialty distributors, specialty pharmacies, and provider networks.

Core Competencies

  • Strategic thinking and execution in market access & reimbursement
  • Strong financial and analytical acumen (pricing, contracting, GTN)
  • Outstanding cross-functional leadership and communication skills
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, patient-focused environment

Travel: 30–50% (to meet with payers, providers, distributors, and field teams)

The Dendreon Way

We are guided by our core values:

  • Put Patients First
  • Act with Integrity
  • Build Trust
  • Raise the Bar
  • Drive Results

If you are passionate about expanding access to life-changing cancer therapies and want to join a high-performing team committed to making the battle against cancer personal, we want to hear from you.

Apply today and help shape the future of immunotherapy.

jobs.description:
Overview

Lynker Corporation is a leading provider of innovative solutions in weather and climate science. With a commitment to excellence and a passion for innovation, Lynker leverages cutting-edge technologies and scientific expertise to support the creation and delivery of improved operational weather forecasts. As part of our ongoing growth and expansion, we are seeking a dynamic and experienced API Developer to join our growing team.

Responsibilities

Duties of the API Developer will include the following:

  • API development: design and build APIs that ingest structured data and serve results to downstream users and applications.
  • Structured outputs: generate versioned, schema-conformant outputs in multiple formats, including PDF and JSON, that faithfully represent the underlying data.
  • Schemas & versioning: define and maintain output schemas, data contracts, and schema and API versioning, using standards such as OpenAPI and JSON Schema, so consumers can rely on stable interfaces as the system evolves.
  • CLI (secondary): provide a lightweight command-line interface over the same functionality for scripted and batch use.
  • Security & deployment: help package and deploy services soundly, applying good practices for access control, dependency management, and compliance in secure or government-adjacent environments.
  • Testing & validation: write unit and integration tests and output-validation checks to confirm results are correct, well-formed, and reproducible.
  • Documentation & collaboration: document APIs, schemas, and output formats; coordinate with the Science and Platform teams that define the underlying data and logic to keep interfaces clear.

Qualifications

The API Developer selected should have the following:

  • Master's in computer science, software engineering, data science, or a related field; or a Bachelor's plus 1-2 years building APIs, services, or data pipelines; or equivalent practical experience, including military or self-taught paths.
  • Proficiency in at least one modern programming language; Python experience is a plus, as it is the likely production language for this work.
  • Experience designing and consuming REST/JSON APIs and working with structured data formats.
  • Understanding of data schemas and versioning, and why stable data contracts matter to downstream consumers.
  • Comfort with Git, Linux, testing, and command-line workflows.

The Ideal API Developer will have the following:

  • Experience generating documents or reports programmatically (e.g., PDF generation) and producing multiple output formats from a single source of truth.
  • Familiarity with schema definition and validation tooling (e.g., JSON Schema) and format versioning practices.
  • Exposure to environmental, geospatial, or scientific data, and formats such as GeoJSON or GeoParquet.
  • Experience with containerization, Infrastructure-as-Code, and CI/CD for reliable, repeatable builds and deployments (e.g., Docker, Terraform or CloudFormation, GitHub Actions).
  • Systems, infrastructure, or networking experience, and familiarity with secure deployment on AWS (e.g., access management, or a security credential such as CC or Security+).
  • Experience with R, including Shiny, or other languages for data apps and rapid prototyping.
  • Familiarity with Rust or an interest in contributing to Rust-based tooling.
  • Colorado Front Range presence for periodic in-person collaboration.

About Lynker

Lynker is a growing, employee owned business, specializing in professional, scientific and technical services. Our continually expanding team combines scientific expertise with mature, results-driven processes and tools to achieve technically sound, cost effective solutions in hydrology/water sciences, geospatial analysis, information technology, resource management, conservation, and management and business process improvement.

We focus on putting the right people in the right place to be effective. And having the right people is critical for success. Our streamlined organization enables and empowers our talented professionals to tackle our customers' scientific and technical priorities – creatively and effectively.

Lynker offers a team-oriented work environment, and the opportunity to work in a culture of exceptionally skilled professionals who embrace sound science and creative solutions. Lynker's benefits include the following:

  • Spot bonuses for exceptional performance

Job Description:

We’re KSM, one of the top 50 largest independent advisory, tax, and audit firms in the United States. But more than our size, it’s our people and culture that set us apart. We believe great things happen when people are supported, challenged, and given the freedom to do their very best work. That’s why we’ve built a workplace where your career and personal life can thrive together – where you have the flexibility to manage your time, the resources to grow, and a team that genuinely cares about your success.

We’ve been employee-owned since 2001, giving every team member a stake in our collective success. This ownership mentality fosters a culture of collaboration, curiosity, and excellence – where new ideas are welcomed, different perspectives are valued, and you’re encouraged to explore what excites you most. Whether you’re expanding your skills, tackling new challenges, or making an impact beyond the office, we provide the resources and support to help you grow in the direction that’s right for you.

At KSM, your contributions matter – not just to the firm, but to your colleagues, clients, and the communities we serve across the U.S. If you’re looking for a place where you can do meaningful work, build lasting relationships, and grow in ways that align with what’s most important to you, we’d love to meet you.

Position Summary:

Katz, Sapper & Miller (KSM) is seeking an accomplished Sales & Use Tax Senior Manager to help lead and expand our growing State and Local Tax (SALT) practice. This is an opportunity for an experienced sales tax professional to make a meaningful impact by combining advanced multistate technical expertise with practice leadership, business development, and team development.

The successful candidate will serve as a trusted advisor to clients, independently leading complex multistate sales and use tax engagements and delivering practical, high-quality solutions to sophisticated technical issues. Equally important, this individual will help shape the future of the practice by strengthening client relationships, mentoring and developing professionals, enhancing processes, championing innovation, and supporting strategic growth initiatives.

We are looking for a collaborative, forward-thinking leader who demonstrates sound professional judgment, intellectual curiosity, and an ownership mindset. The ideal candidate is passionate about building high-performing teams, identifying opportunities to improve how we serve clients, and contributing to the continued evolution and long-term success of KSM's Sales & Use Tax practice.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead and manage sales and use engagements performed within the SALT Group, and ensure accurate and timely deliverables while providing strategic oversight
  • Exercise sound judgment in managing day-to-day client matters independently while appropriately escalating strategic or high-risk issues.
  • Create an environment where managers, seniors, and staff are challenged, coached, and developed into future leaders through meaningful feedback, delegation, and mentoring
  • Develop and enhance their own technical understanding of SALT specialty areas
  • Foster a collaborative, inclusive culture within the SALT practice while strengthening relationships across service lines to increase awareness of SALT capabilities and enhance client service.
  • Serve as Firm technical resource for multistate sales and use tax issues
  • Lead sales and use tax practice initiatives, process improvements, and service offerings.
  • Collaborate across service lines to identify integrated client solutions and expand existing client relationships
  • Champion continuous improvement by evaluating emerging technologies, AI tools, and workflow enhancements that improve quality, efficiency, and the client experience
  • Represent the firm through speaking, publications, and professional organizations.

Requirements/Qualifications:

  • Keep abreast of SALT developments nationwide; communicate to Firm.
  • Develop and enhance excellent technical knowledge, writing skills and verbal communication skills; interpret, complete and review opinion papers, protest documents, internal technical communications, etc.
  • Perform complex tax research; manage tax research projects; utilize managers, seniors and staff when appropriate.
  • Develop deep understanding of client business and industries to provide solutions to SALT related issues
  • Develop and advise on strategies to minimize sales and use tax burden of clients
  • Assist with business restructuring projects with a significant SALT component.
  • Manage state and local tax audits; demonstrate ability to advocate client positions in audit and other potentially adversarial settings with state and local government officials while maintaining positive relationships with government personnel and directing client communications to set expectations.
  • Build and maintain relationships with peer government officials for assistance with various client issues; develop and maintain relationships with professional colleagues within the tax community.
  • Demonstrate the ability to generate high-quality work under deadlines and within budgets; outstanding ability to multi-task within and outside of the firm and across multiple clients, assignments and staff to meet often tight deadlines
  • Manage the economics and profitability of projects.
  • Become an integral part of the technical and professional development of staff; serve as a formal and informal mentor to managers, seniors and staff.
  • Participate in public speaking on technical topics to internal and external audiences.
  • Embrace and promote technology-enabled service delivery, including AI tools and automation, to improve efficiency, quality, and scalability across the practice.
  • Collaborate with Partners and Directors to expand existing client relationships, identify new business opportunities, develop referral networks, participate in community and industry activities, and contribute to the long-term strategic growth of the practice.

Leadership Competencies:

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Strong professional judgment and accountability
  • A positive, collaborative leadership style
  • An ownership mindset with a bias toward action
  • Intellectual curiosity and continuous learning
  • Comfort operating in an evolving, growth-oriented environment
  • Ability to develop future leaders through coaching and mentoring
  • Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence
  • Entrepreneurial thinking balanced with practical execution and risk management

Required Experience:

  • A minimum of 10 calendar years of state and local tax experience, demonstrating a proven progression in complexity of tax issues addressed.
  • CPA or CMI preferred.
  • Proficiency in complex state and local tax research.
  • Bachelor's or master's degree in accounting and/or taxation, or advanced degree (e.g., law degree) and related work experience.
  • Minimum of forty hours of continuing professional education is required each year to maintain and develop technical and business skills.
  • Demonstrated experience leading, mentoring and developing high-performing teams
  • Proficiency in use of tax compliance software, legal research software, and suite of Microsoft Office programs.

jobs.description:
About Kyra

Kyra is an enterprise influencer marketing platform working with brands like SharkNinja, Coach, H&M, Ray-Ban, and Converse. Our platform manages the full lifecycle — creator discovery, campaign management, content review, payments, analytics, and AI-powered intelligence across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.

The Opportunity

You will build Kyra's growth engine from scratch. We run two businesses that feed each other: a profitable managed-service agency that has won enterprise brands for years, and a subscription platform backed by proprietary creator and trend data.

Nobody owns growth across both sides yet, or makes them compound into each other. That is your job. You own the full funnel, run constant experiments, and find the fastest, cheapest ways to win and keep brands. But this is not a traditional growth marketing role, and we are not looking for a traditional marketer. Marketing channels can be learned. What cannot be taught is the instinct to deconstruct a problem, automate the mechanical parts, and build the tools that make one person move like a team.

If you have built a tool, a plugin, a workflow, or an automation that replaced something you used to do by hand — even if you had never written code before — you are who we are looking for. Whatever you did before matters less than how fast you learn and what you build.

Greenfield role with a real budget and a number you own end to end. If you want a clean slate, a live product, and total ownership, read on.

What You'll Do

Own the Number. Active brands is yours: subscribed brands running at least one live campaign in a rolling 30 days. Real usage and real revenue, not vanity signups. For the first 90 days the proxy is qualified leads while you build the pipeline. By year one, active brands is what you answer for.

Build Before You Scale. Before you spend a pound on ads, you build the measurement layer: tracking, dashboards, baselines. None of it exists yet. You instrument the funnel so you know exactly where it leaks, then you fix the leaks before you pour more in. You do not fool yourself with the numbers.

Invent the Channels. There is no channel plan to inherit and no fixed list to run. Paid, organic, lifecycle, AI search, partnerships, things that do not have a name yet — you develop new channels and new ideas, spin up a test in any of them in a day, read the data honestly, and kill what does not work. The mix a year from now should contain things nobody at Kyra has thought of today.

Build the Loop. This is the centre of the role. The agency feeds the platform with warm, high-intent brands. The platform deepens those relationships and frees the agency to win more. Each brand makes the next one cheaper. Build the referral mechanics, the agency-to-platform motion and the data flywheel so growth compounds instead of restarting every quarter.

Build Your Own Tools. This is what separates the role from every other growth job. When you see a repetitive process — ad creative generation, lead scoring, reporting, competitive monitoring — you do not file a ticket with engineering. You sit down with Claude Code or Cursor and build it yourself. A skill that writes ad copy against your brand voice rules. An agent workflow that generates 100 creative variants from a spreadsheet. A pipeline that pulls the data you need into a dashboard every morning. The tools you build are force multipliers. They are how one person moves like a team.

Feed Insight Back into Product. You sit closest to the funnel and the data, so you see what would actually move growth. Surface it. Find the levers inside the product itself: ways to make sharing and referral native, ways to pull more creators in and keep them active, the bits we should change to grow faster. Growth here is as much a product input as a channels job.

What We're Looking For

We would rather hire someone who can learn marketing in months than someone who arrives with a fixed playbook and applies it regardless of fit. The list below reflects that.

Required

  • Builder instinct. You have built at least one internal tool, automation, or workflow that replaced a manual process. We will ask you to walk through how you deconstructed the problem, what you built, and what it saved. This matters more than your channel list.

  • Deep AI proficiency — beyond chat. Not "I use ChatGPT for copy." You build stored, reusable workflows: custom skills, agents, chained tools. You encode your expertise into systems that compound over time. You ship things with Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent, and you know how to orchestrate LLM APIs into pipelines. You treat AI as infrastructure, not an assistant.

  • A track record of moving a number, with the evidence to prove it. Acquisition, conversion, retention, revenue — you have moved a metric yourself, hands on the levers rather than managing from a distance.

  • Fast, honest experimentation. Clean hypotheses and clean A/B tests, with a real grasp of sample size and significance. You scale winners and kill losers without sentiment — including your own ideas.

  • Adaptability. Tools and ways of working change constantly here. You learn new domains and new tools in days, and you would rather work out the right approach than reapply the last one.

  • Spreadsheet modelling. CAC, payback, funnel maths, cohorts.

  • London-based or able to travel in regularly. We want you in and around the team.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Coding — Python or JavaScript to wire systems together and automate the boring parts.

  • SQL, to pull and analyse warehouse data yourself.

  • Paid channel depth (Google, Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn) — budget management, CPL and CPA.

  • B2B, influencer/creator, or two-sided marketplace experience.

  • SEO and AI search optimisation depth.

Traits That Matter

You deconstruct your own workflow before you try to optimise it. Creative. Self-starting. Comfortable with ambiguity. Product-minded as well as channel-minded.

You build the system, not only run it. You form strong hypotheses and kill the weak ones without sentiment. You do not need rigid processes or hand-holding. Tools and ways of working change constantly here, and you thrive on that. A blank page excites you.

What Success Looks Like

Month 3: Measurement layer built from nothing — dashboards, funnels, baselines. Qualified leads pipeline is built and baselined. At least two acquisition experiments are live with clean tracking. You have built at least one tool or automation that made you measurably faster. CAC is baselined and you can already name the biggest leaks.

Year One: Active brands are growing at the agreed run-rate. CAC payback is under 12 months on at least one proven, repeatable channel. Net revenue retention is above target, proving the loops work. You have a ranked view of which channels to scale and which to cut. A growing library of tools and workflows you built that compound your output.

Why This Role

You get ultimate freedom to build, proprietary creator and trend data nobody else has, a two-sided business with real activation levers, and the founders behind you. You build the engine and drive it from day one.

Benefits

🌎 Location: London-based, hybrid. 3 days per week in-office, 4 days during your first two weeks so you get the most out of onboarding and if Europe based then remote but occasional travel to London as part of the role.

🌴 Annual Time Off: 25 days PTO + bank holidays, 4 company-wide days off (Kyra Days), 3 wellness days, and paid sick leave each year.

📚 Growth: Annual Learning & Development budget to invest in your skills.

💰 Rewards: Annual bonus scheme to recognise great work.

🩺 Healthcare coverage for US-based team members.


AI is core to how we operate. Use it to elevate your work. But everything in your application should reflect your own judgement and experience.

💟 Support

If you have a condition or require an adjustment to our interview process - please let us know so we can make adjustments to support you. Please note that when you submit an application or resume, your data will be processed in line with our privacy policy.

Backed by a global team of ambitious builders, problem-solvers, and innovators, we foster a high-performance and fast-moving environment where talent is empowered to drive real impact at the global scale. Supported by 24/7 multilingual customer service and a strong commitment to innovation, we are shaping the future of finance through technology, collaboration, and bold execution.
Today, Bybit is recognized as one of the most trusted and transparent platforms in the digital asset industry, continuing to expand its global presence while building the infrastructure for the next generation of financial services.

Role Overview

This role is to oversee the company’s risk control operations with a keen eye for identifying potential risks. Conduct routine inspections and case analyses to uncover typical fraud risks, refine fraud patterns and characteristics, and propose risk control optimization recommendations.

Key Responsibilities

Risk Tickets Review:

  • Evaluate materials submitted by users flagged for potential risk.
  • Based on submission quality and approval rates, propose optimization suggestions to improve the review process, drive enhancements in review tools, and reduce unnecessary work orders.

Case Analysis:

  • Utilize operational analysis tools to identify fraud cases, analyze fraudulent methods, reconstruct attack chains, and accurately characterize fraud patterns.
  • Provide targeted prevention and mitigation strategies.

Monitoring & Warning:

  • Monitor risk trends, strategy effectiveness, and operational workflows.
  • Build risk early warning capabilities to proactively identify potential threats, enabling more efficient risk perception and control through a combination of operational measures and strategic deployments.

Cross-Functional Collaboration:

  • Work closely with business, product, technology, legal, and compliance teams to embed risk controls into business processes and new product launches, ensuring alignment across departments.

Key Qualifications

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, or related fields.

Experience:

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in risk management, with a background in finance, fintech, or consulting. Prior experience in case analysis, risk review, or related roles is required

Technical Skills:

  • Proficient in data analysis tools such as Hive, SQL, and Excel

Risk Control Expertise:

  • Familiarity with risk control operations and fraud analysis methodologies. Understand key breakthrough points in fraud detection and possess the ability to rapidly deploy and validate risk strategies.

Soft Skills:

  • Strong logical thinking and risk sensitivity, with the ability to quickly identify fraud patterns, reconstruct cases, summarize characteristics, and drive improvements in operational tools and products.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills to align cross-functional teams and drive project success.
  • Passion for risk management with a commitment to continuous learning about industry trends and technologies.
  • Meticulous attention to detail, strong accountability, and resilience under pressure.

Why Join Us
At Bybit, we are committed to fostering a supportive and enriching work environment.

Our benefits include:

- Study Growth Fund: We support your professional development and continuous learning.
- Internal Events: Participate in regular team-building activities, workshops, and events designed to promote collaboration and innovation.
- Global Collaboration: Be part of a diverse, international team, working alongside colleagues from around the world.

As our ASO Specialist and owner of App Store Optimization across Fortis's portfolio for a 6-month contract term, you'll drive how our games show up across the App Store and Google Play, influencing everything from first impression to install. Working across titles in soft launch and global launch, you'll combine creativity, experimentation, player insight, and performance thinking to improve how players find, understand, and engage with our games.

This is a hands-on role with meaningful ownership from day one. You'll build and evolve experimentation frameworks, test new ideas, and partner closely with product, marketing, creative, and game teams to improve store performance across the portfolio — stepping in to run ASO execution while the Product Marketing team scales the function. From icons, screenshots, videos, and copy to keyword strategy and custom store experiences, you'll help shape the moments that connect players with our games.

We're looking for someone who enjoys turning signals into action, challenges assumptions through testing, and can be effective from day one — this role needs minimal ramp-up given the contract term.

What you'll achieve

  • As ASO Specialist, you will own ASO execution across the Fortis portfolio for the contract term, including keyword strategy and metadata optimization
  • Build and run custom store experiences using Custom Product Pages (CPPs) and Custom Store Listings (CSLs)
  • Run A/B tests on store assets — icons, screenshots, video, copy — and translate results into next steps
  • Improve conversion rate across multiple titles simultaneously through structured experimentation
  • Integrate AI-driven workflows into ASO execution for keyword optimization, competitive analysis, and experimentation
  • Partner with UA, Creative, and Product Marketing to align store strategy with acquisition and positioning
  • Connect ASO decisions to broader growth strategy — not treat store performance as a standalone metric
  • Contribute from week one — minimal ramp-up expected given the contract term

What you'll need to be successful

  • Cross-platform ASO fluency across App Store and Google Play is essential
  • Hands-on experience managing ASO for mobile apps or games, including CPPs and CSLs — non-negotiable
  • Proven track record in managing ASO across multiple products simultaneously
  • Specific, measurable conversion rate improvement examples — not just "ran tests"
  • Fluency running experiments from hypothesis to execution to analysis, not playbook-dependent
  • Active AI fluency in day-to-day ASO workflows — repeatable use of AI tools for keyword clustering, competitive analysis, or A/B test reporting, not occasional use
  • Analytical and creative hybrid — reads performance data and translates it into creative direction
  • Background in mobile gaming or large-scale app ecosystems; CET (timezone) overlap strongly preferred for day-to-day collaboration

Why join us

There are many reasons to join us, but here are a few:

  • We strongly believe we are changing how games studios operate and at the core of what we do is making great games that create a connected community
  • We're not just about making Games Where You Belong. We're also about building communities where our people belong. That's why Fortis is a thriving environment that celebrates diversity, embraces inclusivity, and fosters growth.
  • Build and grow with a seasoned team of accomplished talent who have left an impactful mark in their disciplines, both in and out of gaming

Help Us Build a Better Way for Rural Healthcare

Every application helps strengthen a growing network of people who are willing to bring their experience, skills, and heart to rural communities.

Willing to Step In When a Rural Facility Needs Help?

Rural hospitals, clinics, and care organizations sometimes need additional support because of staffing shortages, leaves of absence, seasonal demand, vacancies, service growth, or unexpected coverage gaps.

Explore Rural Healthcare Opportunities at RSSJobs.org

This application may connect you with the specific opportunity you were viewing, as well as other current or upcoming rural healthcare positions throughout Wyoming that align with your experience and goals.

Visit to explore additional rural healthcare opportunities and communities.

Rural Staffing Services is building a trusted network of nurses, technologists, therapists, technicians, and other healthcare professionals who may be interested in short-term, contract, temporary, or permanent opportunities throughout Wyoming.

Whether you are available for several weeks, several months, occasional assignments, or the right long-term opportunity, we would love to learn more about you.

Opportunities May Include

This application may connect you with current or upcoming opportunities such as:

  • Registered Nurse
  • Licensed Practical Nurse
  • Certified Nursing Assistant
  • Medical Assistant
  • Surgical Technologist
  • Sterile Processing Technician
  • Radiologic Technologist
  • CT Technologist
  • MRI Technologist
  • Mammography Technologist
  • Ultrasound Technologist
  • Medical Laboratory Scientist
  • Medical Laboratory Technician
  • Phlebotomist
  • Respiratory Therapist
  • Physical Therapist
  • Occupational Therapist
  • Speech-Language Pathologist
  • Rehabilitation Assistant
  • Pharmacy Technician
  • Behavioral Health Professional
  • Social Worker
  • Other licensed, certified, or experienced healthcare support roles

How You May Help

Responsibilities will depend on the organization, department, profession, and length of the assignment and may include:

  • Providing dependable coverage during staffing shortages or employee leave
  • Supporting patient care and department operations
  • Working alongside permanent employees and local leadership
  • Helping stabilize schedules and reduce pressure on existing teams
  • Supporting rural facilities during recruitment or leadership transitions
  • Assisting with new services, seasonal demand, or periods of increased patient volume
  • Bringing specialty experience to a team with limited local resources
  • Helping maintain safe, timely, and accessible care
  • Completing required documentation and following organizational policies
  • Supporting quality, safety, and regulatory standards
  • Building respectful relationships with patients, employees, and community members
  • Considering permanent employment when the opportunity and community are the right fit

What You Will Bring

Qualifications will vary by opportunity, but organizations may seek:

  • Current licensure, certification, registration, or eligibility as required for the profession
  • Relevant clinical, technical, therapy, or healthcare support experience
  • Strong communication, reliability, and professional judgment
  • The ability to adapt to a new environment and work collaboratively
  • A patient-centered and team-focused approach
  • Willingness to support a rural hospital, clinic, or care organization
  • The ability to meet background, health, credentialing, and onboarding requirements

Opportunities may include:

  • Short-term coverage
  • Temporary assignments
  • Contract engagements where legally appropriate
  • Direct temporary employment with the healthcare organization
  • Part-time or occasional coverage
  • Permanent employment
  • Temporary-to-permanent opportunities

Wyoming's rural healthcare organizations serve communities surrounded by mountains, high plains, ranchlands, rivers, open roads, and wide-open spaces.

These organizations may have smaller teams and fewer nearby resources, which means one experienced professional can make an immediate and meaningful difference.

Helping a rural facility during a staffing gap can support an entire team, protect patient access, and give a community the time it needs to build a more permanent solution.

You will always have the opportunity to decide whether a specific position or assignment is right for you.

Your information will be handled professionally and confidentially.

jobs.description:
Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

In a consumption-based business, revenue isn't won at contract signature—it's earned every day. That makes Finance a critical strategic partner, sitting at the center of the decisions that drive growth, profitability, and customer success. In this role, you'll work directly with executive leaders to influence pricing, structure complex deals, guide capital allocation, and shape the metrics that define business performance. If you're looking for a role where your insights directly impact company strategy—not just reporting results after the fact—this is it.

The Senior Director of Finance – Consumption Business Partner is a senior finance leadership role within Lumen, serving as the primary finance partner to the Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) for consumption-based revenue and reporting into Business Finance. This is one of the most analytically demanding and commercially influential finance roles in the business: revenue is inherently variable, forecasting is a competitive advantage, and — unlike seat-based SaaS — there is no clean ARR number to anchor the plan. Revenue is a function of what customers actually use.

This position partners closely with the CRO leadership team, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Customer Success, Product Finance, COGS finance and the enterprise consumption-modeling (Data Finance) team to ensure commercial decisions are grounded in sound financial analysis. The role focuses on forecast narrative, pipeline-to-consumption conversion, customer and segment risk & opportunity, deal economics, and go-to-market efficiency — translating enterprise model outputs and usage economics into clear commercial implications, trade-offs, and recommendations.

The overriding objective is to enable better CRO decisions and forecast explainability — on deals, pricing guardrails, and go-to-market investment — by turning complex consumption dynamics into a clear financial narrative and actionable recommendations.

Work Location

This is a work from home position within the U.S.

The Main Responsibilities

Main Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary finance partner to the CRO and CRO leadership team for consumption-based revenue, and act as the finance voice in major commercial decisions.
  • Translate enterprise consumption forecasts and usage economics into commercial insights, forecast narratives, and action plans across segments, customers, pipeline, and go-to-market motions.
  • Provide finance support on pricing guardrails and deal structures without owning enterprise models, product assumptions, or cost foundations.

Forecast Narrative, Planning & Business Reviews

  • Translate enterprise consumption forecasts into CRO forecast narratives and rolling outlooks spanning committed ARR, consumption run rates, draw-down schedules, and overage projections.
  • Lead monthly business reviews (MBRs) with CRO leadership, providing insight into consumption trends, forecast risks, and plan variances.
  • Apply committed-to-consumed revenue bridges to quantify gaps between contractual commitments and expected revenue consumption, and explain key drivers.
  • Analyze the pipeline-to-commitment-to-consumption conversion path, identifying where bookings are strong but consumption is lagging.
  • Partner with Revenue Operations to ensure CRM, usage, and financial data align and support a consistent commercial narrative.

Performance, Customer & Segment Analytics

  • Own customer- and segment-level revenue risk and opportunity analysis, translating usage-health signals into quantified financial impacts.
  • Maintain portfolio health KPIs, including consumption rates, draw-down velocity, overage revenue, usage NRR, consumption churn, and usage-based LTV.
  • Identify early warning signs of consumption risk and quantify revenue impact before churn events occur.
  • Deliver cohort-level analysis on consumption growth, usage contraction, and overage-driven expansion while differentiating structural and seasonal trends.
  • Partner with Customer Success on usage-health scoring and post-sale consumption strategies.

Deal Economics, Pricing & GTM Efficiency

  • Serve as the CRO's finance partner on consumption-based deal structures, including committed-spend floors, overage rates, discount tiers, and draw-down terms.
  • Model the economics of large deals to assess whether commitments align with expected usage.
  • Support pricing-model evaluations, including pure consumption, hybrid, and tiered usage models, along with ASC 606 revenue-recognition considerations.
  • Maintain discount guardrails and approval thresholds in partnership with Sales Operations and Legal.
  • Provide financial insights on GTM efficiency, including CAC payback, usage-driven expansion, seller productivity, and demand-generation ROI.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Leadership

  • Collaborate with Revenue Finance, Product Finance, Data Finance, and COGS teams to maintain a single, integrated financial perspective.
  • Partner with the CRO and HR to design compensation plans and SPIFs that align seller behavior with consumed revenue.
  • Contribute revenue organization insights to executive, senior leadership, and Board materials through enterprise FP&A processes.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor, influencing commercial decisions through data-driven analysis and storytelling.
  • Drive continuous improvement of consumption-finance processes, tools, and analytical capabilities.

What We Look For in a Candidate

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
  • 12+ years of progressive experience in financial planning and analysis, business finance, or commercial finance, including senior-level business partnering.
  • Direct experience with consumption-, usage-based, or hybrid pricing models, and building or leveraging usage-based revenue forecast models.
  • Prior experience supporting a revenue, sales, or commercial organization (e.g., CRO), including exposure to deal-desk or commercial-finance structures.
  • Strong analytical and financial modeling skills, including dynamic, scenario-based forecasting.
  • Excellent communication and executive presence, with the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders with data-driven insights and translate financial concepts for non-finance audiences.
  • Strong data fluency and experience working with large usage datasets.
  • Solid understanding of ASC 606 revenue recognition, including variable consideration, usage-based contracts, and pre-purchase arrangements.
  • Proficiency with financial systems and tools such as Excel, Power BI, and CRM platforms (e.g., Salesforce).
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, matrixed environment with strong adaptability, collaboration, and results orientation.

Preferred

  • Experience in cloud infrastructure, data platforms, API-first, or other consumption-based businesses.
  • SQL skills and familiarity with usage-data platforms and data warehouses, including Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery.
  • Experience with complex contract structures, including committed spend, overages, and draw-down mechanics.
  • Familiarity with consumption-based sales compensation and quota-attainment models.

Full-Time| Remote | Flexible, On-Demand Hours

Join our community of 25,000+ professionals building meaningful careers with leading international companies.

About the Company You'll Be Working With

You'll be joining a high-energy, fast-growing European consumer brand in the drinks space — with a strong digital presence, a passionate customer base, and a culture that genuinely cares about experience. This is a lean, dynamic team where your work has a direct and visible impact.

The Opportunity

We're building a bench of German-Speaking Customer Service Agents to support the brand's DACH customers during peak periods. This isn't a standard fixed-hours role — it's a flexible, on-demand arrangement built around the brand's busiest moments.

Here's how it works: agents are guaranteed a baseline of 40–60 hours per month, scheduled as needed around campaign activity. The brand runs a campaign every month, so there's regular, predictable work — plus bigger seasonal peaks like Black Week and the pre-Christmas period, where demand (and hours) increase further. Agents who are open to picking up additional hours during these spikes will have the opportunity to do so.

This is a live chat-only role. You won't be on the phone — but you will be the face of the brand in writing, so strong written German is just as important as your customer service instincts. You'll be handling customer enquiries, resolving complaints, and making sure every interaction reflects the brand's standards.

Because the work is concentrated around campaign bursts (typically 1–2 weeks at a time), we're looking for agents who are genuinely available and responsive during these windows, even if the exact days and hours have some flexibility.

If you take pride in clear communication, stay calm when things get busy, and know your way around an ecommerce environment — we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Handling customer enquiries and complaints via live chat — professionally, promptly, and in German

  • Flexing your availability up during campaign peaks, including monthly campaigns and seasonal peaks like Black Week and pre-Christmas

  • Resolving issues with empathy and efficiency, ensuring customers feel heard and helped

  • Representing the brand's voice accurately across every interaction

  • Identifying recurring issues or patterns and flagging them to the wider team

  • Keeping records accurate and up to date

  • Collaborating with internal teams where needed to resolve customer issues end-to-end

What We're Looking For

  • Native or near-native German speaker — this is a firm requirement; all customer communication is in German

  • Excellent written German — clear, warm, and professional; this will be assessed during the interview process

  • Prior experience in an ecommerce environment — you understand how online retail works and what customers expect

  • Some background in customer-facing communication, whether via chat, email, or phone

  • Calm under pressure and comfortable handling complaints or difficult interactions with professionalism

  • Genuinely available for on-demand scheduling — comfortable with a flexible, campaign-driven workload rather than fixed weekly hours

  • Able to commit to a baseline of 40–60 hours per month, with openness to additional hours during peak periods

  • Reliable and self-motivated — you manage your own schedule and follow through on your commitments

  • Comfortable working remotely and independently within a structured team environment

What's On Offer

  • Competitive hourly rate (discussed during the interview process)

  • Fully remote position — work from anywhere

  • Guaranteed baseline of 40–60 hours per month, with the opportunity to pick up more during peak periods

  • Flexible scheduling within each campaign window

  • Paid annual leave

  • Exposure to a fast-moving, high-growth consumer brand

  • Access to The Global Talent Co.'s wider professional community of 25,000+ global professionals

jobs.description:
Wyoming Rural Healthcare Finance and Revenue Cycle Leadership Opportunities

Rural Staffing Services partners with rural hospitals, clinics, public hospital districts, and community healthcare organizations throughout Wyoming to identify experienced finance and revenue cycle leaders who understand the unique realities of rural healthcare.

We are currently connecting with professionals who may be interested in active and upcoming finance, accounting, reimbursement, revenue cycle, billing, coding, and patient financial services leadership opportunities across Wyoming.

These opportunities may include leadership within Critical Access Hospitals, rural and community hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, Federally Qualified Health Centers, public hospital districts, long-term care organizations, and integrated rural healthcare systems.

Explore Rural Healthcare Opportunities at RSSJobs.org

This application may connect you with the specific opportunity you were viewing, as well as other current or upcoming rural healthcare positions throughout Wyoming that align with your experience and goals.

Visit to explore additional rural healthcare opportunities and communities.

This Is More Than a Finance Role

Strong financial and revenue cycle operations help protect healthcare access for an entire rural community.

These leaders ensure organizations can accurately capture revenue, manage resources responsibly, support employees, maintain compliance, and remain financially strong enough to continue caring for the people who depend on them.

In a rural healthcare organization, finance and revenue cycle leaders often work across departments and may have broader responsibilities than they would in a larger system. The strongest leaders understand how registration, coding, billing, reimbursement, patient accounts, accounting, and operational decisions connect to one another.

They are collaborative, detail-oriented, approachable, and able to turn complex financial information into practical guidance for employees, department leaders, executives, and governing boards.

Opportunities May Include

This application may connect you with current or upcoming roles such as:

  • Controller
  • Assistant Controller
  • Finance Director or Manager
  • Accounting Director or Manager
  • Revenue Cycle Director or Manager
  • Patient Financial Services Director or Manager
  • Patient Accounts Manager
  • Business Office Director or Manager
  • Billing Director or Manager
  • Coding Director, Manager, or Supervisor
  • Health Information Management revenue cycle leadership
  • Reimbursement Director or Manager
  • Chargemaster or Charge Description Master leadership
  • Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable leadership
  • Payroll leadership
  • Senior billing, coding, or patient accounts supervisory roles

What You May Lead

Responsibilities will vary by organization and position and may include:

  • Leading accounting, finance, revenue cycle, billing, coding, or patient financial services functions
  • Supporting accurate and timely financial reporting
  • Managing month-end and year-end close processes
  • Developing budgets, forecasts, and financial performance reports
  • Strengthening billing, collections, cash flow, and reimbursement performance
  • Monitoring key revenue cycle metrics and identifying opportunities for improvement
  • Supporting accurate coding, charge capture, claims submission, and payment posting
  • Overseeing patient accounts, financial counseling, and collection processes
  • Ensuring compliance with payer, regulatory, accounting, and documentation requirements
  • Preparing for financial, coding, billing, or compliance audits
  • Developing policies, procedures, workflows, and internal controls
  • Training and supporting finance and revenue cycle employees
  • Collaborating with clinical, operational, IT, HIM, and executive leaders
  • Helping employees understand how their work affects organizational sustainability
  • Supporting system implementations, process improvements, or departmental restructuring

What You Will Bring

Qualifications will vary by opportunity, but organizations may seek:

  • Progressive experience in healthcare finance, accounting, revenue cycle, billing, coding, reimbursement, or patient financial services
  • Previous leadership experience as a director, manager, controller, supervisor, or comparable leader
  • Knowledge of healthcare reimbursement, payer requirements, billing practices, and financial operations
  • Experience with Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and patient-pay accounts
  • An understanding of hospital, clinic, or healthcare-system workflows
  • Experience analyzing financial or revenue cycle performance and communicating findings to leadership
  • Strong organizational, problem-solving, and team-development skills
  • Experience with Critical Access Hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, FQHCs, public hospital districts, or community healthcare organizations
  • Relevant education or professional credentials based on the position
  • A collaborative and relationship-focused leadership style

Some opportunities may prefer credentials such as CPA, CHFP, CRCR, CPC, CCS, RHIA, RHIT, or other finance, coding, revenue cycle, or health information certifications. Requirements will depend on the specific role.

Why Rural Wyoming?

Wyoming's rural healthcare organizations serve communities surrounded by mountains, high plains, ranchlands, rivers, open roads, and wide-open spaces. These organizations frequently operate with lean teams, limited resources, and a tremendous responsibility to the communities they serve.

Finance and revenue cycle leadership in a rural organization provides the opportunity to see the direct impact of your work. Improving a process, supporting a team, or strengthening reimbursement can help preserve services, protect jobs, and keep care available close to home.

Join the RSS Rural Talent Network

By applying through this page, you are joining the confidential Rural Staffing Services talent network. You may be considered for current or upcoming finance and revenue cycle leadership opportunities that align with your background, goals, location preferences, and availability.

Please include your resume and let us know:

  • Which Wyoming communities or regions you would consider
  • Whether you are open to relocation
  • Whether you are interested in permanent, interim, remote, fractional, or multiple types of opportunities
  • Which areas best match your experience, such as accounting, finance, billing, coding, reimbursement, patient accounts, or full revenue cycle
  • Your experience with rural hospitals, Critical Access Hospitals, public hospital districts, FQHCs, or community healthcare organizations
  • Which position or community you were viewing on RSSJobs.org

Our team personally reviews each application. When we identify an opportunity that may be a strong match, we will contact you directly to share more about the organization, community, responsibilities, and next steps.

Your information will be handled professionally and confidentially.

Work Where It Matters.

Built for Rural.

Despite this, there’s been very little innovation over the past 70 years in how materials - which constitute up to 40% of project costs - are bought and sold. This is our opportunity.

About Kojo

It's time to build. Whether it's creating more housing, upgrading our infrastructure, or adapting to climate change, one thing is clear: the construction industry is at the center of solving our biggest problems. We're making buildings cheaper and easier to build by transforming the way commercial construction companies buy their materials. Join us.
